newsitem.title: JAPAN: China's TITIC mulls samurai bond issues - sources.
newsitem.headline: China's TITIC mulls samurai bond issues - sources.

text.p: China's Tianjing International Trust and Investment Corp (TITIC) is considering launching about 13 to 15 billion yen worth of samurai bonds by the end of 1996, underwriting sources said on Thursday.
"TITIC had contacted several underwriters and expressed its desire to raise funds by issuing samurai bonds," one underwriting source said.
"TITIC is wishing to issue approximately 13 to 15 billion yen (worth of the samurai bonds), with a duration of five to seven years," another underwriter said.
However, other underwriters said there was still a possibility that TITIC might not issue samurai bonds if the cost of raising funds through the samurai market was too high.

They said there was a case this year in which Guangdong International Trust and Investment (GITIC) was considering issuing samurai bonds but ended up raising funds through Yankee bond issues. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8785
